records.claim: TechBench Labs independent benchmark (dated 2026-08), setup: 1 KB messages, fsync per batch, replication factor 3, 6 nodes, p99 latency target < 50 ms. StreamCore 4.0 sustained 220,000 msg/s at 38 ms p99.
records.applicability: This is the only measurement in the sources that matches the target workload (1 KB, durable, RF3, 6 nodes). 220,000 msg/s is below the 300,000 msg/s requirement.
records.limitations: The excerpt is very short. It gives no hardware specs, client or producer config, batch size, acks or consistency level, test duration, number of runs, funding or sponsorship. 'fsync per batch' may not match the requester's durability semantics. It is a single source, and a web search found no other trace of TechBench Labs.

records.claim: In the same benchmark, QueueForge 2.3 sustained 410,000 msg/s at 61 ms p99. It achieved 340,000 msg/s with p99 < 50 ms.
records.applicability: QueueForge exceeds 300k msg/s in steady state with no failures. At the benchmark's 50 ms p99 target, the margin is 340k vs 300k. At 61 ms p99, it is 410k.
records.limitations: The 410k figure misses the benchmark's own 50 ms p99 target. The 50 ms target comes from the benchmark, not the requester, who gave no SLO. The p999 figure and the test duration are not reported. Steady state only: no failure or rebalance scenario was tested.

records.claim: StreamCore was CPU bound on replication in the TechBench test.
records.applicability: This suggests faster or more CPU cores, or replication tuning, might raise StreamCore's throughput. No source quantifies how much, so closing a 36% gap (220k to 300k) on 6 nodes is unsupported.
records.limitations: CPU model and core count are not stated. Whether tuning was attempted is not stated.

records.claim: StreamCore vendor blog (2026-04-02): StreamCore 4.0 sustained 1,000,000 msg/s on a 3-node cluster with 100-byte messages, in-memory mode (persistence disabled), replication factor 1.

source.title: StreamCore 4.0: one million messages per second (vendor blog)

records.applicability: This is not comparable to the requirement. The payload is 10x smaller, there is no persistence and no replication, and the cluster has 3 nodes. It confirms the assumption that the 1M figure is not evidence for a durable 1 KB RF3 workload.
records.limitations: This is vendor marketing with no methodology beyond one sentence. It predates the independent benchmark (April vs August 2026). It only conflicts with E1 on the headline number, not under matching conditions.

records.claim: Arithmetic on E4: 1,000,000 msg/s x 100 B is about 100 MB/s of payload with no durability or replication. That is about one third of the target's 300 MB/s ingest (300,000 x 1 KB) before any replication.
records.applicability: This supports discounting the vendor claim.
records.limitations: Derived calculation. The plan says not to recompute in research, so this is flagged for the analysis stage to confirm.

verification.method: Simple unit arithmetic on fixture values

records.claim: QueueForge 2.3 operations guide: rebalancing after node loss can take 10-20 minutes at high partition counts, during which throughput may drop up to 40%.
records.applicability: A worst-case 40% drop from 340k-410k would give about 204k-246k msg/s, below 300k, for 10-20 minutes. Whether this applies depends on partition count ('high partition counts' is not defined) and on whether the requirement must hold during failures.
records.limitations: 'Up to' 40% is a ceiling, not a typical value. 'High partition counts' is not quantified. There is no curve of impact versus partition count or data volume. No independent measurement of failure behaviour exists for either broker. StreamCore's failure behaviour is undocumented.

records.claim: QueueForge recommended max partitions per node: 4,000.
records.applicability: On 6 nodes, the ceiling is about 24,000 partition replicas (or 20,000 on 5 surviving nodes). No source states the partition count needed for 300k msg/s, so the analysis cannot tell whether that ceiling is near the 'high partition counts' that trigger long rebalances.
records.limitations: It is unclear whether the limit counts leader partitions or all replicas.

records.claim: QueueForge licence: open source (Apache 2.0); commercial support optional.
records.applicability: Answers the QueueForge side of C6.

records.claim: StreamCore licence, support and cost terms are not documented in any supplied source, and a web search found no product by that name.
records.applicability: C6 cannot be scored for StreamCore.
records.limitations: The web search for StreamCore broker licensing returned only unrelated products (Lightstreamer, HiveMQ, streamco.org).

records.claim: Requirement as stated by the user: sustain 300,000 durable (persisted, replicated) 1 KB msg/s on at most 6 nodes. The user gives no latency SLO, replication factor, acks level, headroom requirement, or whether the rate must hold during failures.
records.applicability: RF3, the 50 ms p99 target and the failure-mode requirement are planner or benchmark assumptions, not user statements.

records.claim: Resource load at the target, assuming RF3: about 300 MB/s ingest and about 900 MB/s cluster-wide writes. On 6 nodes that is about 150 MB/s disk writes per node and about 100 MB/s replication egress per node (each leader sends 2 copies of its 50 MB/s share). On 5 surviving nodes, about 180 MB/s writes per node.
records.applicability: These bandwidths are within reach of modern NVMe and 10-25 GbE hardware. The planned target hardware is unknown, so whether 6 nodes is physically realistic cannot be confirmed.
records.limitations: Arithmetic from the request and the plan's RF3 assumption. Ignores protocol overhead, consumer egress and rebalance traffic. No hardware specs are available from the requester or the benchmark.

records.claim: No external information exists online for StreamCore 4.0, QueueForge 2.3 or TechBench Labs. Web searches returned only unrelated brokers and benchmarks (meshIQ 2026, SoftwareMill mqperf, OpenMessaging Benchmark, Solace).
records.applicability: The supplied documents are the only evidence. Independence and reproducibility of the benchmark cannot be checked externally. A proof-of-concept on target hardware is the only way to close G1, G3 and G4.
records.limitations: Search snippets only. WebFetch was not attempted because the environment blocks it.
